questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Career opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Australia is an English-speaking country with a lot to experience both academically and culturally while having both similarities and differences to what I'm used to in Denmark.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Before the introduction from the exchange coordinator from USYD it could be challenging to find the information I needed. Afterward, the information provided in mails was sufficient and the ability to receive answers to questions from the coordinator also made it easier.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didn't really need any more than what was provided in general which was enough for me.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was quite difficult and expensive but I travelled with my partner which made the process a bit easier since we were able to pay more than one single person. We ended up living in various Airbnb's which worked fine for us. It was expensive but from what I have heard from other Danish exchange students in Sydney we each paid the same as everyone else had to do.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: If you want to meet international students from other countries than Denmark I would recommend living on campus but you get a better feeling of the actual city by living off campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process worked fine with several steps carefully explained. It began in good time and necessary explanations were available.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Excel sheet with an overview of all possible units of study, before this was sent it was more challenging and time-consuming to find units of study and to check if I was eligible

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got what i hoped for but had to make a change after the time table could be seen since to of my units overlapped.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I recommend applying for up to 10 different units of study even though you only need 4. You might not get all requests accepted and after the time tables get out you might need to make late changes due to overlaps.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took first-year MA units at USYD even though I was a second-year MA student at UCPH and it worked fine.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Pretty similar but I had classes taking place in the evening and with more students than i was used to.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
ITLS5020 Production and Operations Management
ITLS5050 Introductory Supply Chain Analysis
QBUS5001 Foundation in Data Analytics for Business
QBUS5015 Foundations of Health and Civic Analytics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: For students with a public health background or similar i would recommend QBUS5015. The two ITLS units are more in the production and supply chain management field i would only recommend

questions.answer: I found it pretty easy, but did also have my partner with me to supportme.

What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The many different kinds of cultures in the country.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
To my expirience as a public health student, USYD isn't the most obvious choice since the units of study related to the Master in Public Health and the Master in Global Health at USYD are all closed for exchange students. Therefore I had to be creative in finding relevant units.
Be prepared to get out of your comfort zone.
Try to meet people from both Australia and other countries, but at the same time meet some other people from Denmark who are going through the same as you

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The experience of living away from home in another country.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Having enough time for all the things you can do.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
